| [CLAIM-174](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-174.md) v8 | A candidate factor is an agent at a level when it is one system there, when a goal-directed description beats a device description by more than the Occam cost, and when its policy would adapt if its actions' consequences changed; it is a willed agent when, further, a will-organization over several regimes describes it better than none, and what passes that is the jurisdiction of a will-organization | The assistant's admission test for the owner's thesis, filed at the owner's request. | [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) | A person's roles in contexts that do not meet cannot contradict one another: role conflict needs an overlap, which segregating audiences prevents and collapsed contexts create | The MoM manuscript models a person's roles ("daughter", "teacher", "friend") as sections over family, professional and social contexts, with identity as their global section, failing when the roles contradict. Conflict needs an overlap: an occasion on which two audiences are present at once. People manage the cover. They segregate audiences, which keeps the contexts disjoint, and they script the occasions where audiences must meet. Broadcast and networked media collapse contexts, which creates overlaps the person did not choose (boyd 2008, after Meyrowitz 1985). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-198](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md) | Preference reversal is not yet disunity: interests that govern a choice at disjoint times glue, and a self is divided over a choice only on an overlap, which the agent's prediction of its own later valuation creates | Take an agent's interests as sections over contexts of choice, each governing the windows of time in which its valuation ranks first. | [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md) v4 | For a communicative kind, the standard of sufficiency is the uptake of competent participants who know the standings and norms in play: a defeasible standard, overridden only where the act's other constituents diverge from the judges' verdicts, so a probe family is tested against it, and a kind outruns the families coarser than that standard and the judges only through those constituents | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-206](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-206.md), and the argument [CLAIM-247](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-247.md) found missing. For an act partly constituted by uptake ([CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md)), competent participants' uptake is that standard, and since version 2 a defeasible one: CLAIM-241 is conceded, so the verdicts yield where the act's other constituents diverge from them. The kind's extension is the class the standard fixes, and analysts' families are insufficient when coarser. No test needs a kind that outruns every family. A proposal, resting on a Proposed premise. It does not touch the ontological clause of CLAIM-204, which superseded CLAIM-139 and keeps that clause, and which the programme does not test. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md) v3 | For a named population of receivers and a stated family of tasks, what survives a translation, retelling or rendering is the set of task-relevant communicative distinctions those receivers can still recover from it, and measured preservation of the pragmatic observables predicts that recovery better than preservation of the wording or of the proposition, with or without its force | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to the audit's objections to the tests of the manuscript's thesis ([CLAIM-233](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-233.md), [CLAIM-232](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-232.md), [CLAIM-243](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-243.md), [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md), [CLAIM-226](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-226.md), [CLAIM-222](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-222.md)). It restates [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) as an empirical claim indexed to receivers and tasks, tested against the rival [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md) itself names, a proposition with its force, on a behavioural criterion and with an interlingual arm that decides. It supersedes [CLAIM-115](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-115.md), by the owner's delegated ruling of 2026-10-29. It is a proposal, not a finding. It does not claim the line's distinctive machinery is needed: that is [CLAIM-202](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-202.md). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-221](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-221.md) v3 | The relational-constitution thesis's defeat condition describes a standard rival the record holds no counter for, intention-based accounts of illocution, which plausibly meet it for every act in the four-speakers case except the institutional one | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) is defeated by a held account that individuates teasing, reproach and reprimand by the utterance plus speaker-internal states. That is the intention-based line of Grice, Strawson and Bach and Harnish, none of whom the record holds. On it [CASE-018](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-018.md)'s friend, parent and comedian differ in communicative intention, and only the judge needs norms, which Searle ([LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) already supplies. The record's own model for [CLAIM-111](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-111.md) is of this family. The objection is open; it would narrow [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) to institutional acts unless an argument from uptake meets it. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-224](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-224.md) | Under partial relational constitution, a translation always changes the participants, audience and norms that the relational-constitution thesis makes constituents of the act, so whether the act survives turns on a correspondence of relations the structure cannot supply from inside | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (structure lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. That makes [QUESTION-005](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-005.md) a question about what the act is, not only how to measure it, and the record's model of translation holds the audience fixed. [CLAIM-138](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-138.md) spares [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md); this applies its point to [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) through translation. | [CLAIM-228](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-228.md) v4 | D_obs restated over a rendering procedure, with one kernel family fitted on some source items and scored on held-out ones and the target term the readers' response averaged over the procedure's output, separates rendering procedures that receivers' task-indexed recovery separates, so restated it measures observational fidelity informatively | The record's repair, on 2026-10-10, of the manuscript's L_obs and the profile's D_obs after [CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md), [CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md) and [CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md). For one pair a constant kernel makes D_obs zero ([CLAIM-207](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-207.md)); fixed across items, it fits only if the target readers' responses do not vary with the item. The repair ties the outcome-level kernels to the text channel, makes the transport a property of a procedure ([CLAIM-230](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-230.md)), and makes deficiency a finite computation over judgement outcomes ([CLAIM-235](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-235.md)). A proposal: the derivation is elementary, but whether the restated measure is informative is the defeat condition's empirical question. It does not say a fitted kernel is the translator's process. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-240](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-240.md) v4 | A holistic fidelity judgement is fidelity under the judges' default task, a weighting of the profile's components that can be estimated on some renderings and tested on others, so it is well defined and consistent with task-relativity, and a defeat condition that uses it must name the population and fix the weighting before the test, and across populations with unequal access to the source must fit the weighting only on the components each can perceive | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md). Task-relativity ([CLAIM-128](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-128.md)) denies a ranking that holds across tasks, not that a population has a default task. A weighting estimated on held-in data and tested on held-out data is a finding, not a fit, and a weighting fixed before the test leaves no room to blame the task after a failure. A proposal: whether holistic judgements are such a weighting is itself empirical. The objection is right that the stated defeat conditions name neither task nor receivers; [CLAIM-220](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-220.md), [CLAIM-204](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-204.md) and [QUESTION-075](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-075.md) address that. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-242](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-242.md) v3 | The use-level counterpart of Saussure's value is an utterance's contrast with the alternatives its speaker could have used in context; values do not cross between languages, which is why fidelity is graded transport through an anchored correspondence rather than identity of value | The record's reply, on 2026-10-10, to [CLAIM-254](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-254.md). It grants the objection's premises: value is internal to one language state, and it is a fact of langue, while the line's observables are facts of use. It denies the conclusion. What the premise rules out is identity of value across languages, which the line does not claim ([CLAIM-106](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-106.md)), and transport through a correspondence fixed from outside both systems is what [CLAIM-082](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-082.md)'s own qualification already requires. At the level of use, contrast with alternatives is the rational-speech-act model's premise ([THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md)) and Bergen, Goodman and Levy's finding ([LIT-809](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-809.md)). Saussure becomes precedent, not premise. A proposal, not a refutation. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-244](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-244.md) v3 | The defeat tests take one holistic, task-free judgement of fidelity as ground truth, though the line's own theses say fidelity is task-relative, interpreter-relative and not a single ranking | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (empirical lens); no turn of the exchange raises it. The theory's measure must then be fitted to that weighting, which is circular, or a mismatch blamed on the judges' task, which leaves nothing that defeats. It does not say the judgements are useless, only that the defeat conditions lack the task and receiver index the line's own theses say fidelity needs. [CLAIM-140](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-140.md) is its neighbour: that one moves the criterion to the analyst, and neither says it is task-free. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-250](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-250.md) v2 | What a developing argument should preserve through legitimate revision is its accountability structure, what was asserted, why, how it was challenged and what justified its revision, not its propositions, so fidelity is defined over justificatory and provenance relations while propositional content changes | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the third open tension ([CLAIM-189](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-189.md) against [CLAIM-252](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-252.md)). | [CLAIM-251](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-251.md) v2 | A change in which questions a receiver population can answer determinately is not by itself a change of cover in the sheaf sense: the cover belongs to the measurement scenario and the responses are an empirical model on it, so such a change is a change of empirical model, which can create or remove a gluing obstruction on a fixed cover but does not change what the cover is, and the operational notion needs its own name until a functorial link is shown | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the open tension between [CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md) with [CASE-048](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-048.md) and the operational cover of [CLAIM-201](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-201.md). | [CLAIM-255](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-255.md) v2 | Intending to perform an act, performing it and being recognized as having performed it are distinct, coupled variables: intended meaning is fixed at production, the act partly by roles, standing and norms, and recognition by uptake, so competent uptake is constitutive for some acts, evidential for others and irrelevant to the existence of still others | From the interlocutor's reading of PR [#121](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/121) and its reconciliation, relayed by the owner on 2026-10-12, on the first open tension ([CLAIM-160](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-160.md) against [CLAIM-151](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-151.md) and [CLAIM-217](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-217.md)). | [CLAIM-258](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-258.md) v2 | Blackwell's order compares experiments about one parameter, so it does not reach the normal translation case: source and target readers decide about situations with changed coordinates, and where the state is common a translator with context knowledge yields a rendering that is not a garbling of the source, which the order typically leaves incomparable with it and about which the direction the manuscript uses is silent | Found in the record's audit of the line on 2026-10-10 (formal and structure lenses); no turn of the exchange states it. Blackwell's order is still defined then, but typically leaves source and target incomparable, and the direction the manuscript uses says nothing. It does not say decision-relative fidelity is wrong. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-262](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-262.md) v2 | Whether an agent's regimes are coordinated by discrete switches or by continuous reorganization depends on how the agent is constituted; both occur | The owner's answer to [QUESTION-079](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-079.md): both forms are possible, and which one an agent shows depends on its constitution. | [CLAIM-263](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-263.md) v4 | Whether two trained networks compute the same way can be tested by quotienting the architecture's full symmetry group and measuring what remains: a barrier that survives alignment marks a different mechanism, connection after alignment means shared feature structure, and the test cannot run where features have no counterpart | The general content of [CLAIM-187](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-187.md), filed alone in learned-structure under [ADR-040](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-040.md): a measured protocol for asking whether two trained solutions are the same solution. Quotient the full symmetry group, including the orthogonal map on a transformer's residual stream ([THEORY-112](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-112.md)). Read a barrier that survives as a difference of mechanism ([THEORY-116](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-116.md)). Between linearly connected image classifiers, nearly every layer's features interpolate ([THEORY-111](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-111.md)). It is the first claim in the learned-structure line. | Proposed |

| [CLAIM-274](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-274.md) v2 | Participation on a shared canvas thins selectively: people keep coming back while art they invested in survives, so unaffiliated corruption falls over the event and the remaining participants are weighted toward maintainers, a cooling schedule the population produces for itself | The owner's correction to [CLAIM-273](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-273.md). So the "temperature" of random corruption is high early and low late. This is a feedback from pattern to flow, and it answers [QUESTION-085](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-085.md) in part. Untested on the logs. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-276](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-276.md) v2 | A shared interpretation's coherence, its fidelity to evidence and the plurality of live alternatives are separate quantities, and a population can raise the first while lowering the other two, so a collective interpretation's stability is no evidence of its truth | A1 §6, before the influence canvas: meaning as "metastable patterns of mutually reinforcing constraints", with the caveat that "delusions, dogmas, and self-reinforcing errors can also become metastable". It does not say coherence is bad. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-281](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-281.md) v3 | Granting influence by role lets a process empower another as a critic while opposing its preferred policy, so an organization that allocates authority by role can keep disagreement working inside it instead of sorting into factions | A2 §8, on the owner's U2 design. Indexing grants by role, E_i(j, r, c, t), lets i back j as an error detector without backing j's authority over the final choice. [CASE-080](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-080.md) is the worked example. It does not say role boundaries hold under pressure. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md) v5 | A grant scheme that denies each operator control over its own authority can make delegation do work: rewarded for how far their preferred policies are realized and not for authority held, operators delegate to aligned others, and the two conditions need not be confined to one-hop allocation | The owner's design at U2 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: operators vote on one another's influence, cannot significantly manipulate their own, and gain by finding aligned operators and delegating authority to them. Under them, empowering a better-placed ally is a way to get one's policies realized without becoming more powerful. It does not say such schemes resist collusion, or that alignment makes delegation wise. | Proposed |

It is the claim [CLAIM-278](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-278.md) objects to. It does not say these processes are a self. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-295](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-295.md) v4 | A record of an inquiry's justifications adds nothing for decisions its current state already suffices for: what it can add is a wider family of decisions for which what is kept suffices, and decisions a bounded agent can make that it otherwise could not | A10's conclusion, with A5's second claim and A10 §5's three values of history: informational, computational and option value. The cases make the first half exact ([CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md), [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md)). The second half, that real inquiries change their questions in ways that make the purchase worth its cost, is not shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md) v2 | A frame can change a judgement by changing which of an interpreter's stored distinctions are reachable, without supplying any evidence about what is being judged | A20's proposed claim, after the owner tied addressing to anchoring at U20, and A19's "addressing conditions". (2019, read) find the most direct measure of the accessibility step does not replicate and cannot detect priming at all. The retrieval step is inferred, not shown. The mechanism the record holds, attention as sparse distributed memory ([LIT-269](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-269.md)), is a model, not evidence about judges. The extension to communication in general is the record's and is not shown. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-301](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-301.md) v2 | Iterative retrieval can turn a provisional interpretation into a premise: a framing selects what is encountered, what is encountered reinforces the framing, and the question being investigated drifts as well as the queries | A21's proposed claim, from the owner's U21 link between retrieval-mediated anchoring, agent harnesses and older information retrieval. Classical IR named query drift ([LIT-1079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1079.md)). An agent that rewrites its own task adds [TERM-056](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-056.md), which A21 judged "arguably more consequential". The exchange did this itself between A2 and A13. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-314](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-314.md) v3 | Reusing a filed argument has a recognition cost that a fixed per-use price leaves out: certifying that stored answers cover a new question is NP-complete even for conjunctive queries, grows with the number and size of the stored definitions rather than being a constant per item, and is undefined for an item filed without a statement of what it answers, so each filing raises the cost of later reuse and per-item break-even decisions are not independent | Filed at the owner's request, from the readings on answering queries using views (Levy, Mendelzon, Sagiv and Srivastava 1995; Chandra and Merlin 1977; Halevy 2001). [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md)'s guarantee needs a fixed, known per-use cost c_a; recognizing that a stored answer covers a new question is a search whose cost depends on everything stored, so filing one item changes the price of using the others. It undermines the premise [CLAIM-308](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-308.md) states, not its arithmetic. The hardness is worst case and over short definitions, partial reuse is cheap, and nothing here is measured on the record. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-315](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-315.md) v3 | In comparative anchoring tasks, considering an anchor shifts the later numerical estimate without adding evidence about the target, and the shift is carried by anchor-consistent knowledge made more accessible; the shift is established, the accessibility step is inferred and has not been measured | The empirical half of [CLAIM-298](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-298.md), split off under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md)'s pilot, which found that claim compound: an empirical claim about judgement tasks and an interpretive extension to communication in general. | [CLAIM-317](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-317.md) v2 | Self-presentations that differ by audience do no harm while the audiences are kept apart; people keep them apart and script the occasions where they must meet, and broadcast and networked media bring them together unchosen, which is when the presentations collide | Split from [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) under [ADR-043](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-043.md): the empirical half of that claim, the sociology of audiences on which its sheaf reading rests. Its evidence is boyd (2008, read in part in [NOTE-710](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-710.md)), after Meyrowitz (1985), and one documented collapse, [CASE-064](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-064.md). boyd's claims about collapse are documented with interviews and examples, not measured, and the Carmichael case reaches the record secondhand, so it stays Proposed. It says nothing about overlaps, covers or gluing; that is [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md)'s. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-327](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-327.md) v2 | A slowly changing collective variable, such as a reputation, a rivalry or a standing, is part of a collective's dynamics and not only an observer's average when its members read it, condition what they do on it, and by doing so regenerate it | A9 §3 and §10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, after Flack 2012 (LIT-1122, unread). | [CLAIM-336](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-336.md) v11 | The pragmatic-transport and will-organization lines describe one model, an organization of operators that act on a shared interpretive state under a context while allocating one another's influence: a frame is the context under which operators act, a judgement is the response they yield, an action-generating regime is an operator or coalition, and a will-organization is the dynamics that allocates influence among them | The owner's, U2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16: the pragmatic-transport model and the will-organization model are "both manifestations of the same underlying model". | [CLAIM-337](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-337.md) v2 | Active inference already runs an internal loop: mental action selects among higher-level cognitive states and sets the precision of lower-level observations, structure learning reshapes the generative model without action, and a judgement is behaviour, so a judgement–observation loop may be action and perception one Markov blanket inward | The assistant's, A1 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on active inference's behalf, strengthened at A4. With Chalmers's point that judgements are behaviour, the owner's judgement is active inference's action relocated. What it does not reach: the diagram. | [CLAIM-338](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-338.md) v5 | The selectivity active inference gives action, sampling what one expects to experience, is played in the coupled meaning–authority model by the authority space: influence decides which operators retrieve and so what the next judgement observes, which makes Friston's self-confirming sampling the model's authority-to-interpretation arrow and his agent a coupled loop run without independent scoring | The owner's, U10 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, on Friston et al.'s "sampling selectively what one expects to experience": "I think this selectivity maps to the authority space in my coupled model." Worked out by A10. Selective sampling is the β arrow of [CASE-099](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-099.md), authority shaping interpretation through what it retrieves. Policies scored on current beliefs are the γ arrow. So Friston's agent runs both arrows, and his "this weakness becomes the strength" accepts capture, with the anchor moved outside the loop to selection on whole agents. | [CLAIM-355](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-355.md) v10 | In a distributed agent the binding of appraisal, readiness and governance into one response can be real while the single owner a self-model or collective self-description attributes it to is a representational construction, not a further entity; the illusion, where there is one, is in the attribution and belongs to whichever system adopts the representation, and this deflates the self without settling whether experience is real | The owner's, U26 and U27 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: at U26 whether, "adopting an illusionist/fictionalist position", the record can make claims about subjecthood; at U27, "illusory binding-type phenomena in distributed agents", starting from the record's emotion material. | [CLAIM-358](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-358.md) v5 | Learned local accommodation can reduce the amortized cost of recurrent arbitration: where a recurring conflict among an agent's processes admits a stable accommodation, settling it among the processes can cost less over repeated encounters than escalating each instance to a higher-level process that mediates or overrides, though local negotiation and the relations it needs are not free | The owner's, U45 of the exchange of 2026-10-17: "processes which can navigate disagreement amongst themselves require fewer resources from the system than processes which need to activate additional subsystems to resolve disagreement." | [CLAIM-393](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-393.md) | Ordinary and legal attributions of agency to an artifact cannot serve as the independent marks that would defeat the record's agency test, because they turn on whether its mechanism is understood: a known mechanism invites "This is all just programmed!", an inscrutable one invites fear, whatever the description lengths | From Boyle's "inscrutability paradox" in The Line ([LIT-1288](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1288.md), read in [NOTE-1014](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1014.md)): if an apparently general AI comes from well-understood programming, people will doubt it has autonomous consciousness, since it is "merely doing or saying that which we have programmed it to do"; if its workings are inscrutable, they will find it "more mysterious and potentially more threatening" (p. 30; pp. 54, 246, 272). | [CLAIM-417](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-417.md) v6 | What the record explained by "self" in its dispositional, persisting, self-governing and integrated senses is better explained by organizational perspectives, with a perspective, its carriers, its lineage and its representations kept apart; the subject sense stays a separate question, and narrative, presented and modeled selves involve representations that may describe a perspective, attribute it to a bearer or construct an owner, none of them the perspective itself | The owner's, at U31 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: the record's earlier "selves" are "better described as 'organizational perspectives'". | [CLAIM-423](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-423.md) v5 | In a political collective, components that change at different speeds (attention, coalitions, elected terms, administrative careers, law and treaties, generational memory) are not only nested by timescale: under a given institutional arrangement their different temporal horizons affect which forms of influence each can accumulate, exercise and keep, and so which of them holds authority over the others, so a state can stay continuous as an actor while the organization producing its positions changes under it | The owner's, at U28 of the exchange of 2026-10-22: domestic and international politics as the domain where "regime ecology" becomes concrete, with "separation of timescales in elections, durations of tenure in elected and appointed positions, lifespan, generational memory, etc." creating "amorphous collectives of varying orders and degrees of coupling". | [CLAIM-431](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-431.md) v4 | A corporation's functional remorse cannot be told from prudence: any procedure or role duty that makes others' harms its concern was put there for its own ends, reputation, liability or recruitment, so the line between harm as concern and harm as threat, and with it the line between a remorseful and a psychopathic corporation, does not hold, and the clinical word adds nothing to a description of its incentives | The objection to the record's reading of the "institutional psychopath", revised on 2026-10-23 when the reading was revised. | [CLAIM-432](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-432.md) v5 | A corporation can be an agent fit to be held responsible and the bearer of functional affect in Frijda's sense, so psychopathy's affective features can be assigned to it as well as its conduct: it lacks remorse, functionally, when harm it does to others is not among the concerns its own appraisals track and gains precedence over what it does only when a regulator or a market turns it into a threat to the corporation's concerns; that profile, threat without remorse, is the construct's, and it is changed by redesigning the corporation's concerns, not its members' characters | The record's reading of Bakan's "institutional psychopath" (LIT-1430, unread), filed at the owner's request on 2026-10-23 and revised the same day when the owner pointed out that the record's framework assigns affect to corporation-like things ([CLAIM-039](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-039.md), reopened). | [CLAIM-433](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-433.md) v2 | The potential account of valence is an account of goal-conduciveness valence, not of intrinsic pleasantness: on the component process model's separation of levels of valence, the ordering that prevails ranks states by need satisfaction and goal attainment, the potential's strength tracks 'wanting' and its sign tracks goal conduciveness, while 'liking' is a separate appraisal with its own ordering; so the wanting–liking dissociation is two valence systems coming apart, as that separation predicts, and the objection that the account is not about pleasure is conceded rather than answered | The reply the owner asked for, 2026-10-23, to the objection that potential tracks 'wanting', not 'liking' ([CLAIM-438](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-438.md)). Shuman, Sander and Scherer's "levels of valence" separate intrinsic pleasantness from goal conduciveness, on Berridge's evidence; Scherer and Moors report that the two have different physiological signatures and combine multiplicatively. | [CLAIM-435](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-435.md) v2 | Veit's common currency and ALARM's override are two regimes of one ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, compensatory and overriding, so their rivalry over what the first felt valence did becomes the question whether the earliest potential orderings are continuous: in motivational trade-off experiments, a continuous indifference curve between a noxious cost and a resource for Veit, a discontinuity at a threshold beyond which no resource buys the cost for ALARM; only a graded override, deciding at every level of its own intensity, lacks a currency altogether | A consequence of the owner's reframing of valence as ordering-potential ([CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md)). [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) records that its rivalry with ALARM "would dissolve if ALARM's "100% weight" were recast as a weight in a common currency rather than an override of it." It is recast instead: both are an ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, compensatory or overriding, and the trade-off test separates them by continuity. Corrected on reading Debreu before filing: a threshold override still has a (discontinuous) currency; only a graded override has none ([CLAIM-436](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-436.md), part 3a). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-437](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-437.md) v4 | 'Wanting' and 'liking' are saliences relative to different, overlapping processes, pursuit and consummation, each ranking states by their bearing on its own concerns; valence is then relative to a perspective, every perspective in the negotiation has its own, the system's valence is that of the perspective whose ordering is the negotiation's potential, and ambivalence is strong saliences of opposite sign with no potential absorbing them | The owner's, 2026-10-23: "maybe 'wanting' and 'liking' can be differentiated by characterizing them as saliencies relative to different (possibly overlapping) processes? | [CLAIM-438](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-438.md) v5 | An ordering serving as the negotiation's potential, as the potential account of valence defines it, tracks 'wanting', not 'liking': sensitized incentive salience wins a system's conflicts, persists and resumes while hedonic impact measured by taste reactivity stays flat or falls, so the regime the account calls hedonic valence is motivational valence, and hedonic valence, if it is anywhere in the account, is elsewhere | Raised by the reading of Berridge and Kringelbach ([NOTE-1110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1110.md)) filed on 2026-10-23 for the potential account. ([NOTE-1111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1111.md)) concede the same of their account, which puts valence in the system's model of its own potential rather than in the potential. | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-439](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-439.md) v5 | A regime of valence is felt, in the sense of attended and available to the system's other processes, when the system that is in it also models it: when a deeper process infers which ordering wins its negotiation, which way the system is moving along it and how strongly it prevails, and the inference is used elsewhere in the system; unfelt valence is the potential without that model, as unfelt fluency is a change in precision without the inference about it | Filed at the owner's direction, 2026-10-23, as a candidate for when the functional regime of [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) is felt. | [CLAIM-440](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-440.md) v5 | An organization's appraisal is the negotiation among its perspectives, a common currency is that negotiation's admitting an ordering of the options it faces, and goal-conduciveness valence is a regime in which an ordering of the organization's own states by their bearing on its maintenance prevails in the negotiation; so valence presupposes contested rankings, not frustrated demands, its sign is whether the organization runs ahead of or behind a reference course along the potential ordering, its intensity is how far the negotiation's decisions follow that ordering, and ambivalence, where no ordering prevails, differs from neutrality, where one prevails and the organization keeps to its course | The owner's, 2026-10-23, in the discussion of [THEORY-101](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-101.md) that followed the corporate psychopathy filing: "what if the 'appraisal' is the process by which competing perspectives negotiate amongst themselves? | [CLAIM-442](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-442.md) v7 | Frijda's emotion and the potential account's system valence sit on opposite sides of the gap between the precedence a motive claims and the authority it is granted: an emotion, action readiness claiming control precedence, is a claim, a perspective's valence is read on its claims, and the system's valence is read on what the negotiation grants, so a change in grants with the claims fixed, as mindfulness is said to make, changes the system's valence and leaves the perspectives' emotions and valences as they were | The assistant's, from a comparison of the record's will and affect lines made at the owner's request on 2026-10-23 and filed at the owner's direction. | [CLAIM-445](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-445.md) v5 | A protective regime, in a person, an institution or a system of states, becomes self-maintaining when the interventions it authorizes shift the evidence used to judge its necessity, the authority and resources of those who judge it, the capacities of its constituents or the threat environment itself in ways that favour its continuation; this can happen when the original threat was real and the first protection apt, and it is a failure only where the regime has become less responsive to evidence that it is no longer needed | The owner's, 2026-10-23, on the account of governance-maintained anxiety ([CLAIM-446](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md)): "this seems like it would also be supported political and social scientific observations about state/societal protectionism". | [CLAIM-446](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-446.md) v8 | Some persistent anxiety may be governance-maintained rather than belief-maintained: anticipated threat grants defensive processes authority over action, attention and evidence acquisition; under the avoidance that authority selects, the hypotheses that the situation is dangerous and that it is safe predict the same observation, so repeated safety need not correct the threat estimate; relief reinforces the defense without being evidence of danger; and the regime can outlast a corrected belief, its pathology, where present, being defensive authority insensitive to corrective evidence at avoidable cost | The owner's, 2026-10-23, quoting "A governance prior can become self-protecting by reducing the access of the processes most likely to provide evidence against it": "I think you may have inadvertently landed on a formalization of anxiety". | [CLAIM-447](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-447.md) v2 | Model-based wanting is a pursuit process's ranking of the futures it predicts under candidate interventions, P(S \| do(a)) against P(S \| do(a₀)), while cue-triggered wanting is learned salience that need not compute those futures; a process's causal model, its wanting and its practical efficacy are separable, so learning to want differently, learning that a want will not pay, and learning not to act on it are three different changes | The owner's, 2026-10-23, asking what the record's account of wanting is: "i just found myself characterizing it as a kind of a prediction about a future state, and realized that really this is a do() operation and the future state that's being anticipated is what might or might not happen given a candidate intervention." | [CLAIM-451](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-451.md) v3 | When an organization's record of winning moves cycles, the failure is organizational nonintegrability, distinct from a perspective's own preference instability and from switching of the governing regime; it becomes organizational tension only when realized as costly reversal against demands the organization maintains, and cognitive dissonance only when that tension is detected and appraised as aversive; learning can relieve it by accommodation, by entrenched precedence or by cheap periodic coordination, which observed coherence does not tell apart, and ambivalence and nonintegrability entail neither one another | The owner's, 2026-10-23, quoting "A potential exists exactly when the finite relation of observed wins is acyclic": "rather than asserting potentials always have to exist, could we characterize cycles as a kind of internal tension or cognitive dissonance? preference/perspective/will instability?" | [CLAIM-514](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-514.md) | World-modeling is a family of resource-bounded capabilities for producing and using predictions about an environment's possibilities and consequences, each relative to a declared family of questions; a world model in the representational sense is one possible realization of them, competent behaviour can determine environmental structure without identifying any internal mechanism, and producing, maintaining and revising world-modeling capabilities are further achievements, not prerequisites of agency in general | The owner's preferred formulation at the second review of the filing of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31). | [CLAIM-519](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-519.md) v2 | Competent behaviour does not establish an internal world model: over a fixed interface and a finite horizon, an agent with no model, whose actions are looked up from the history so far, reproduces the interaction distribution of an agent that has one exactly; a policy can identify predictive structure without any particular internal component realizing it, so compression and generalization support comparing candidate architectures, and establishing an internal mechanism needs evidence that discriminates candidate implementations, such as targeted interventions | The owner's thesis at U20 of the exchange "Analyze nucleation concepts" (2026-10-31): that under the record's framework a world model is "essentially a 'folk' explanatory tool and that no such thing need explicitly be present for the external behavior to be indistinguishable from a comparable black box agent which actually did contain a world model". | [CLAIM-527](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-527.md) v2 | Viable reach, valence and emotion are three quantities in an organization, not one: an emotion is a claim to precedence, system valence is movement along the ordering that wins the negotiation, and a change in what the organization can viably reach is neither, so an organization can run ahead along its prevailing ordering while its viable reach contracts | Filed 2026-10-31 from the readings of Massumi and McKim (2009) and Bencherki, Brummans and Vézy (2024). | [CLAIM-541](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-541.md) v2 | Wu-wei is better read as control placed and timed where a system's own dynamics do most of the work than as the absence of control: Ott–Grebogi–Yorke control of chaos is a formal instance, in which small perturbations timed by the system's own wandering hold it on an unstable orbit, and the control, though small, continues for as long as the orbit is held; so reported effortlessness has at least three distinct sources, no conflict to override, conflict settled cheaply by learned accommodation, and conflict met as it arises by small well-timed feedback, which may feel alike and differ in mechanism | The owner's U17 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02), quoting A16 on Ott–Grebogi–Yorke control: "that's very wu-wei". | [CLAIM-544](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-544.md) v4 | If a willed agent is the jurisdiction of its will-organization, then governing one's own governability is in part governing one's own individuation, in the constitutive sense of individuation at that level: a revision of the will-organization that changes which regimes it governs changes which willed agent there is, so a self-forming revision can be a re-individuation and not only a change in an agent's states, and whether the revised jurisdiction continues the earlier agent is a question of continuation, not of resemblance | The join the owner's U31 of the exchange "Assess SDT Coverage" (2026-11-02) asked for, "connect to individuation", made through the owner's own entry for it, [CLAIM-170](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-170.md), which A31 never cited. | [CLAIM-603](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-603.md) v6 | A capability lost because another reliably supplies it is the Black Queen's loss, favoured to the one who loses it, and whether it is dependency or division of labour is decided by the supply, not the loss: one-way supply set from outside, as aid is, leaves a dependence that nothing in the dependent's dynamics limits and that withdrawal punishes, while reciprocal loss, each partner supplying what the other gave up, leaves interdependence, so the aim framed as self-sufficiency is better framed as reciprocity | The assistant's, on the owner's remark of 2026-11-05 that "assured help makes recipients lose skill" sounds "closely related to niche differentiation and specialization phenomena". On the Black Queen Hypothesis ([THEORY-1048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1048.md)) a cell that stops making a leaky public good saves its cost while others still supply it, so the loss is favoured to the individual and spreads. Buchnera ([THEORY-1103](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1103.md)) has lost the genes its host covers and kept those its host lacks. The Samaritan's dilemma has the same logic (Ostrom et al.), and Azam, Devarajan and O'Connell's recipient is better off in the high-aid state. The loss itself is not the pathology. What differs is the supply. A Black Queen loss stops by itself when helpers grow rare, because the helpers are the same population. Buchnera's loss runs both ways, and the result is interdependence. A state that taxes its citizens (Moore) is in the same position: it lost nothing, it exchanges. | [CLAIM-606](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-606.md) v5 | A localized structure can persist by an internal balance that needs no supply, by a balance of gain and loss that needs a standing supply, or by a topological charge that continuous change cannot remove, and the three differ in what carries the structure's identity, how it forms and how it ends; because thresholds and abrupt ends appear in all of them, even with no supply at all, only withdrawing the supply and measuring the outflow tells which route a structure is on | The assistant's, after the owner's hunch that "the physics/dynamics of soliton formation could be a valuable angle through which to consider some of our questions about individuation and persistence". | [CLAIM-859](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-859.md) | In two distinct mechanisms that mix a structured step with a uniform one, preferential attachment or copying with a uniform share and noisy sample-space reduction, the tail's survival exponent is one over the structured share | Two mechanisms the record now holds readings for mix a structured step with a uniform one. In attachment with a uniform share (Mitzenmacher, [THEORY-2150](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2150.md); Barabási's directed copying is the same formula, [NOTE-2270](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2270.md)), a new link goes to a uniformly chosen node with probability α and by degree otherwise, and the degree density falls as k^−(2−α)/(1−α), so the survival exponent is 1/(1 − α). In noisy sample-space reduction (Corominas-Murtra et al., [THEORY-2175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2175.md)), a step is nested with probability λ and uniform otherwise, occupation falls as i^−λ in rank, and the frequency exponent is 1 + 1/λ, so the survival exponent is 1/λ. In both the survival exponent is one over the share of structured steps: structure alone gives the marginal exponent 1, and the uniform share sets how far the tail is diluted from it. This is a pattern across two mechanisms, offered as a candidate row for [QUESTION-505](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-505.md), not a theorem; whether it reaches past processes of this mixed form is not shown. | [CLAIM-865](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-865.md) | Where a support acts on an assembly only by changing its transition rates and is withdrawn for good, the drop in the chance of completing when it is withdrawn at a state equals the expected total, along the course the supported assembly would take from that state, of how much the support changes each rate times how much the unsupported chance of completing turns on that step; for a support that holds a nucleus this is the nucleus's fragility times its worth, so the assembly becomes independent of the support before it is complete only where what it has built holds the nucleus or no longer needs it | The assistant's, from carrying out [LEAD-095](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-095.md). A's measure for [QUESTION-398](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md) is D(s) = q_supported(s) − q_withdrawn(s). On the transient states, Q_S(q_S − q_0) = −(Q_S − Q_0)q_0, so D(s) is the expected integral, along the supported path from s, of the support's rate changes weighted by the unsupported committor's differences across them. That is a standard perturbation identity for absorption probabilities; its use here is the record's. Three things follow. The chance after withdrawal depends on the state reached alone, so all the support leaves behind is the state. For a scaffold that holds a nucleus the integrand is the nucleus's dissolution rate times Δ_N⁰ = q_0(with nucleus) − q_0(without), so D becomes small before completion only where the units built hold the nucleus or the nucleus has stopped mattering. And where neither happens, the support is needed until completion however far assembly has gone. In [CASE-308](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-308.md)'s model D falls below 0.05 a quarter of the way through when bound units stabilize the nucleus, and stays at 0.10 or more to the last unit when they do not. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

Implication does not remove the linear directions. Every attribute is read out exactly, by an affine map, from the full-rank spectral embedding, and the recovered incidence and its concept lattice equal the generating ones. What implication changes is the spectrum. On a balanced b-ary tree, the eigenvectors are branch contrasts rather than one per attribute. A branching at depth ℓ gives eigenvalue μ_ℓ = w Σ_{ℓ′>ℓ} λ_ℓ′ b^(D−ℓ′), with multiplicity (b−1)bˡ, and these fall strictly with depth for any positive strengths. So a rank-(b^K − 1) embedding reads out exactly the attributes of depth at most K. Below the cut, each attribute's readout is the same constant on every descendant of its depth-K ancestor, so siblings merge. That holds for ordinary mixture-of-experts gating and for a load-balancing loss added to it. | [CLAIM-937](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-937.md) | Contextuality-by-Default signalling has no unbiased estimator at any finite count, but it has a confidence interval and a no-signalling test that are valid at every count, and a content seen at most twice in each context can never be found signalling by a valid 5% test | Derived for [LEAD-072](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-072.md) on 2026-11-22 and checked by exact enumeration and simulation ([CASE-359](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-359.md)). A learner whose residual obeys ė = −Ae, with A symmetric positive semidefinite (kernel gradient flow, or any network under gradient flow on squared loss, with A its tangent kernel over n), and levels P_ℓ summing to the identity. Against the flow under Σ P_ℓ A P_ℓ, in which no level talks to another, level ℓ's relative residual departs by at most ‖[A, P_ℓ]‖/(λ_ℓ s_ℓ) at any time, λ_ℓ being the level's slowest rate and s_ℓ its share of the initial residual; the constant cannot be improved. It follows that each acquisition time lies in an interval, that the symmetric order survives any perturbation of the operator below a threshold proportional to the rate gap, and that below a risk of about that ratio squared the slowest mode sets every level's time, so the times converge in ratio. For a moving operator the same holds with the commutator integrated against the level's own decay, a sharper form of A2's ∫‖[A_t, P_ℓ]‖dt. Checked in [CASE-358](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-358.md). The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

In two-hidden-layer ReLU MLPs on a two-cue task, the barrier left after alignment falls with width for every kind of pair. At width 5, pairs that rely on the same cue keep barriers (0 to 0.65 in loss) that overlap those of pairs relying on different cues (0.15 to 0.54), even after an exhaustive search over permutations and rescalings. From width 64, both kinds are connected. Within a width, the barrier falls as the matched units' activations correlate more. Permutations alone leave a barrier between two copies of one function that differ by per-unit rescaling, and quotienting rescaling removes it. A trained curve joins aligned endpoints that the straight line does not, both across the board and in the one flat, poorly connected cell of a load-by-temperature grid, where the accuracy deficit stays. So in this toy, connectedness after alignment is a property of width, of the symmetry group and of the path family, more than of the mechanism.
